Welcome. I’m glad you’re here, ready to explore a journey that asks us to look deeper—at ourselves, at our relationships, and at the world around us.
Have you ever wondered how the legacy of white supremacy quietly shapes the everyday—sometimes out in the open, sometimes in subtler ways we barely notice?
Layla F. Saad’s book, Me and White Supremacy: Combat Racism, Change the World, and Become a Good Ancestor, invites us to step into that honest reckoning. She calls us to examine not just society, but our own lives—urging us to question where privilege, bias, and complicity show up, often without us even realizing.
This isn’t just about pointing out what’s wrong or sitting in discomfort. Instead, it’s about transformation—opening ourselves up to new awareness, empathy, and a real sense of responsibility. Together, we’ll look at how self-reflection and true accountability can reveal the real roots of racism—not as something tucked away in history, but alive and immediate, something we have the power to challenge and change.
Along the way, we’ll discover that this process isn’t about feeling guilt or shame, but about finding the courage to face tough truths and the hope that comes from genuine change. When we start to peel back those internalized beliefs, a path opens—a path that leads us toward becoming better ancestors, toward shaping a world that’s more just and compassionate for everyone.
So, as we step into this exploration together, let’s stay curious, courageous, and open to the possibility that what we learn here could ripple out—touching our communities, and maybe even changing the future.
